claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure consisting of fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The FeCoNiTi system shows ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Coexistence of the C14 phase changes the magnetic ground state of the fcc phase through an interphase interaction.
The C14 phase is Ti-rich, whereas the fcc phase is Fe/Co-rich.
Antiferromagnetic coupling develops between the Ti-rich C14 phase and the Fe/Co-rich fcc phase.
Ti atoms at the fcc/C14 interface mediate antiparallel spin alignment.
The C14 phase may be antiferromagnetic or paramagnetic with induced magnetic moments.
Antiferromagnetic interphase coupling reduces the net magnetic moment and saturation magnetization attributed to the fcc phase.
The C14 phase has high magnetic anisotropy.
Fcc/C14 phase boundaries act as strong domain-wall pinning sites.
C14-phase anisotropy and interfacial domain-wall pinning impede domain-wall motion and thereby increase coercivity.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because their orbital moments are insufficient.
Dual-phase FeCoNiTi is predicted to reach approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K.
Dual-phase FeCoNiTi is predicted to have lower fcc-phase saturation magnetization than a pure-fcc counterpart.
The proposed mechanism requires a thermodynamically stable C14 phase and a coherent or semi-coherent fcc/C14 interface.
The mechanism may fail if the C14 phase is amorphous or the Ti concentration is too low to induce antiferromagnetic coupling.
The Ti-coupling mechanism is extrapolated from Cr-associated antiferromagnetic interactions and Mn-associated magnetic frustration in other high-entropy alloys.
A spin-polarized interfacial DFT calculation is proposed to evaluate the fcc-phase spin density of states at the Fermi level, local moments, and antiparallel spin alignment.
Magnetic hysteresis at 400 K should be compared among dual-phase, C14-dominant, and preferably single-phase-fcc control specimens.
The hypothesis is falsified if DFT finds no meaningful interfacial antiparallel alignment or moment reduction, or if dual-phase coercivity at 400 K is at most 100 Oe.
